title: WebAuthn
subtitle: Hardware-key sign-in for the person who approves an OAuth grant, on an alternate entrypoint of the server, with the assistants' path left unchanged.

stats.label: before the locking change was reverted

lede: Auth and access plane is the OAuth server through which commercial AI assistants and my own agents get access to my tool estate. The control point there is a person approving each grant on a consent screen. I added WebAuthn hardware-key sign-in to an alternate entrypoint of that server, so the person approving a grant can be asked to prove presence with a security key or platform authenticator instead of a password. The open-source python-fido2 library handles the FIDO2 protocol. My work is the flow around it. A visitor who reaches the authorize endpoint unauthenticated is sent to a login page. Registration binds a credential to the user.
quote: A person's consent is the control, and a stricter gate nobody can pass weakens the system.
evidence: OAuth and identity architecture: WebAuthn hardware-key sign-in for the person who approves an OAuth grant, returning them to the exact grant they were approving.
Security design: login challenges that expire after 300 s, and a registration lock reverted because it locked out every legitimate assistant.
author: Corey James
